newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude prices up with WTI, Maya talked.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude prices up with WTI, Maya talked.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices rose sharply Tuesday, amid trader concerns that cancelled deliveries of Colombian crude would tighten supply into the U.S, traders said.
But sales of Alaska North Slope (ANs) crude -- the West Coast regional benchmark -- remained flat. Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under West Texas Intermediate.
Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude rose to $17.55/17.71 a barrel, in line with higher cash prices in the rest of the U.S.
Light crude Line 63 also rose with WTI, while its discount remained steady at minus $3.05 a barrel, and its price over Buena Vista stood unchanged at 90 cents to $1.00.
State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) sold a 360,000 barrel cargo of Maya heavy crude to a Los Angeles refinery late last week, market sources said.
Traders said Shell bought a cargo of Maya for its Martinez Calif. refinery , near San Francisco, earlier and that the shipment was en route.
Mobil and Ultramar also expected to finalize spot or term deals for the Mexican crude within a week.
Overall, five cargoes were expected to be delivered with the next two months, traders said.
Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudess -- California heavy grades -- were flat after major oil companies lowered postings late Monday.
